title: Cache telemetry v2 — draft notes / open questions (prefix + KV cache)
body:
Doc intent (working draft)
- This is the rough working area for v2 prefix/KV cache telemetry. Confluence will hold the finalized spec + ADR.
- Audience: runtime instrumentation (Omar/Samir), control plane attribution (Ethan/Amara/Mina), telemetry pipeline (Nadia/Caleb/Mei), SRE dashboards/alerts (Sergio/Sean/Rafael), Optimize recs (Aditya).
- Goal: trustworthy hit-rate + savings metrics + enough attribution to debug and to generate Optimize “increase hit-rate” recommendations, WITHOUT exploding metric cardinality.

Non-goals (for v2)
- Not changing cache algorithm behavior (eviction, admission, etc.).
- Not building ML-driven recommendation model (heuristics only).
- Not perfect customer-facing UI polish.

Quick glossary (terms we keep mixing)
- prefix cache: cache keyed by token prefix (typically request prompt prefix) to skip prefill work.
- KV cache: cached attention keys/values for prefix tokens; “hit” implies some amount of prefill avoided.
- prefill: forward pass for prompt tokens.
- decode: forward pass for generated tokens.
- cache lookup: runtime checks if prefix exists.
- cache insert: runtime stores KV blocks for a prefix.
- partial-prefill: request needed to run prefill for some tokens because only part of the prefix was cached.
- fragmentation: same logical workload splits across routes/models/versions so cache doesn’t warm effectively.

Key outcomes we need from v2 (requirements)
1) A single authoritative hit-rate definition that matches savings (saved prefill) for most workloads.
2) Hit-rate can be broken down by:
   - tenant
   - route
   - model + version
   - region
   - deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
   …but with cardinality guardrails (hashed IDs / “top-K + other” aggregation).
3) We can answer: “Why did my hit-rate drop?”
   - traffic mix shift vs instrumentation/attribution bug vs cache policy mismatch vs fragmentation.
4) We can answer: “Did cache help latency + cost?”
   - saved prefill milliseconds (and optionally saved tokens) as primary.
5) We can compute: “cacheable prompt ratio” (how much traffic could benefit if normalized/pinned).

Draft definitions (please comment; these are NOT final)

A) Outcome classification per request (intent: align metrics + recs)
- cache_outcome (enum):
  - HIT: request prefix fully served from cache (no prefill for cached prefix tokens).
  - PARTIAL: some prefix tokens reused but some prefill still executed for prompt tokens.
  - MISS: no usable prefix cache.
  - BYPASS: cache disabled or ineligible (policy, size limits, model unsupported, etc.).
  - ERROR: cache path errored (should be rare; treat separately).

B) What counts as a “lookup”
- A cache lookup occurs when runtime evaluates eligibility and attempts to find a matching cached prefix.
- If policy marks ineligible BEFORE lookup (e.g., prompt too large, cache disabled), do not increment lookup_total; instead increment bypass_total with reason.

C) Hit-rate primary definition (for dashboards)
- hit_rate = hit_requests / (hit_requests + partial_requests + miss_requests)
  - Excludes BYPASS and ERROR from denominator by default.
  - Rationale: we want a “how good is the cache given eligible traffic” metric.

D) Secondary hit-rate (sometimes needed)
- eligible_rate = (hit+partial+miss) / (hit+partial+miss+bypass)
- overall_hit_rate = hit / (hit+partial+miss+bypass)
  - Useful for “why do I see 5% hit-rate?” cases where 70% of traffic is ineligible.

Metric candidates (names are draft; align to Confluence later)
NOTE: We should decide if we ship these as counters + distributions, then derive in dashboards.

1) Core counters (per minute rollups)
- redwood.cache.lookup_total
  - increments when a lookup is performed (eligible path).
- redwood.cache.outcome_total{outcome=HIT|PARTIAL|MISS|BYPASS|ERROR}
  - per request classification outcome.
- redwood.cache.bypass_total{reason=policy_disabled|prompt_too_long|model_unsupported|private_mode_restricted|other}
  - alternative to stuffing reason into outcome_total.
- redwood.cache.insert_total
- redwood.cache.evict_total{reason=capacity|ttl|manual|other}

2) Savings / impact (primary for “does it matter”)
- redwood.cache.hit_bytes_total
  - bytes of KV blocks reused (or logical bytes). Need to standardize units.
- redwood.cache.saved_prefill_ms_total
  - estimated ms of GPU work avoided due to cache reuse.
- redwood.cache.prefill_ms_total
  - observed prefill time for eligible traffic (for context and sanity checks).

3) Traffic characterization (for recommendations)
- redwood.cache.cacheable_prompt_total
  - count of requests whose prompt would be cacheable under policy if normalized/pinned (definition TBD).
- redwood.cache.prompt_prefix_len_tokens_bucket{bucket=...}
  - optional distribution to understand prefix lengths and cacheability.
- redwood.cache.prompt_hash_bucket_total{bucket_id=...}
  - only if we decide we need prefix clustering; must be aggressively bounded.

4) Errors / correctness
- redwood.cache.instrumentation_dropped_total{reason=sampled_out|cardinality_guard|payload_too_large}
- redwood.cache.attribution_missing_total{field=tenant|route|model|region|deployment_mode}

Tagging / attribution (draft)
Hard requirement: every event/metric must be attributable enough to drive drilldowns.
Hard constraint: cardinality budget.

Proposed required tags (for rolled-up metrics)
- deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private
- region: e.g., us-east-1, eu-west-1 (bounded list)
- model_family: e.g., llama, mistral, qwen (bounded-ish; still needs governance)
- model_id: Redwood internal stable model id (bounded; but can still be large)
- model_version: short string OR “pinned/latest” + build id (risk: cardinality explosion)
- tenant_tier: free | pro | enterprise (bounded)

Proposed optional tags (with guardrails)
- tenant_id: allow only on sampled / aggregated metrics (see below)
- route_id: allow as hashed + topK only (see ADR-027 draft)
- project_id / workspace_id: likely NO for v2 due to cardinality

Two-tier telemetry approach (draft; likely direction)
- Tier 1 (always-on, low cardinality): global + region + deployment_mode + model_family (maybe model_id).
  - used for fleet health dashboards and alerts.
- Tier 2 (sampled + guarded): adds tenant_id + route_id + model_id + model_version.
  - used for customer drilldowns, regression debugging, and Optimize recs.

Sampling (draft)
- Default sampling for Tier 2: 1% requests, with per-tenant adaptive sampling for “top tenants by volume” up to 10%.
- Always include all traffic for “outcome_total” if we can keep tags low cardinality.
- If we do request-level structured events: sample at 0.1% globally + “burst capture” on regression triggers (SRE-only; time-bounded).

Cardinality guardrails (draft notes; Nadia/Thomas to validate)
- route_id strategy: “route_key_hash” with bounded bucket count per tenant/region (e.g., 256 buckets) OR top-K routes + other.
  - open: do we actually need route_id raw? probably not.
- tenant_id: allowed only in Tier 2; enforce max distinct tenants per region per hour before aggregating into “tenant=other”.
- model_version: dangerous; propose model_variant (pinned vs latest) plus “runtime_build” instead of full version string.
  - open: Optimize wants model version fragmentation detection; we can do it via control plane logs instead of metric tags.

Saved prefill ms: estimation approach (rough)
- In runtime, on lookup HIT/PARTIAL we estimate saved_prefill_ms as:
  saved_prefill_ms = (cached_tokens * prefill_cost_per_token_estimate)
  - where prefill_cost_per_token_estimate is derived from recent observed prefill performance for that model/hardware.
- Risks:
  - will drift with batching and load.
  - needs to avoid “double counting” when partial-prefill occurs.
- Alternative: compute savings as (observed prefill_ms_without_cache_baseline - observed prefill_ms_with_cache) but baseline is hard in production.

Notes from runtime discussions (unpolished)
- Omar: do NOT add heavy logic to hot path; compute outcome classification with minimal branching.
- Samir: can produce per-request outcome + token counts; anything beyond that should be aggregated asynchronously.
- Marcus: overhead budget target <1% at p95 for typical prompt length distributions.

Dashboard drilldowns we want (examples)
These are the concrete “questions” that should be answerable in Console / internal Grafana.

1) Global cache health
- Time series: hit_rate (eligible) by deployment_mode + region
- Time series: saved_prefill_ms_total by deployment_mode + region
- Table: top model_families by miss_rate + bypass_rate

2) Tenant drilldown (Enterprise support/Solutions)
- Filter: tenant_id
- Breakdown: hit_rate by route (topK) and by model_id
- Overlay: eligible_rate (to see if policy is preventing cache)
- Correlate: saved_prefill_ms/request and p95 latency

3) Route / feature drilldown (internal)
- Filter: route_id_hash bucket (or route_id if we ever allow raw)
- Check: cacheable_prompt_ratio (proxy) to identify prompt normalization opportunities
- Check: prefix_len distribution to see if prefixes are too short to matter

4) Regression diagnosis
- Compare last 30m vs previous 24h baseline
- Segment by:
  - region
  - model_id
  - runtime_build (important!)
- Show “attribution_missing_total” to catch instrumentation breaks
- Show “instrumentation_dropped_total{cardinality_guard}” to catch tag explosion

5) Optimize recommendations evidence (minimum viable)
- For a given tenant_id + route_id:
  - “Routing fragmentation suspected”: hit_rate low + many model_id/model_variant combinations seen + small volume per combination.
  - “Prompt prefix diversity high”: high cacheable traffic but low repeat prefix buckets (needs hashed clustering signal).
  - “Cache policy mismatch”: bypass_rate high with reason=policy_disabled or prompt_too_long.

Open questions / decisions needed (tracking)

Q1: Do we need a request_id anywhere in telemetry?
- Leaning NO for metrics (cardinality). Maybe only in sampled structured events with strict cap.
- Use trace_id correlation for debugging when explicitly enabled.

Q2: How do we represent model version without cardinality explosion?
- Options:
  1) model_variant = pinned|latest + runtime_build (bounded-ish)
  2) model_semver (high risk)
  3) do version fragmentation analysis offline in logs/events (not metrics)
- My vote: option (1) for metrics; option (3) for detailed analysis.

Q3: “Partial” semantics: where’s the cut line?
- If cached_tokens == 0 => MISS
- If cached_tokens >= prompt_tokens => HIT
- Else => PARTIAL
- Need to confirm behavior under:
  - streaming retries
  - tool-calling multi-turn where system prompt is same but user prompt differs
  - multi-route fallbacks

Q4: What is “cacheable prompt ratio” exactly?
- Candidate definition: ratio of requests that (a) are eligible by policy AND (b) have prefix_len_tokens >= MIN_PREFIX_FOR_VALUE.
- Alternative: requests whose first N tokens match a canonicalizable template (requires clustering; too heavy for v2).
- We likely ship a proxy now and rename if needed.

Q5: Should BYPASS be in the hit-rate denominator?
- Default for dashboard: exclude BYPASS (eligible hit-rate).
- For customer-facing interpretation: we must show eligible_rate alongside hit_rate to prevent confusion.

Q6: Private deployments constraints
- Do we have uniform region tag semantics for on-prem?
- Proposed: region=customer_site_id (bounded per customer; but then cardinality??)
- Might need “region=private” and “site_id” only in customer-local telemetry.

Q7: How do we prevent a repeat of “hit-rate doesn’t match latency savings”?
- Require both outcome metrics AND savings metrics.
- Add validation panel: saved_prefill_ms/request should trend with hit_rate; if diverging, flag known issues (partial-prefill counting, retries).

Examples (pseudo query math)
- eligible_hit_rate = sum(outcome_total{HIT}) / sum(outcome_total{HIT|PARTIAL|MISS})
- eligible_rate = sum(outcome_total{HIT|PARTIAL|MISS}) / sum(outcome_total{HIT|PARTIAL|MISS|BYPASS})
- avg_saved_prefill_ms_per_req = sum(saved_prefill_ms_total) / sum(outcome_total{HIT|PARTIAL|MISS})
- bypass_share_by_reason = sum(bypass_total{reason=*}) / sum(outcome_total{HIT|PARTIAL|MISS|BYPASS})

Known pitfalls (write down so we don’t forget)
- Tag explosion via route/model_version/tenant_id combinations.
- “Model routing fragmentation” can look like cache regression; need dashboards to show route/model mix explicitly.
- Retries: a retry might be counted as an additional MISS but the user perceives single request; decide if we tag retry_attempt.
- Partial-prefill: if we count as HIT for lookup but still run prefill, savings will not match.

Short-term next steps (week 1 targets)
- Logan: converge metric names + definitions with Allison (Observability standards) and write Confluence v2 spec.
- Nadia/Thomas: propose explicit cardinality limits and enforcement mechanism (drop vs aggregate).
- Omar/Samir: confirm hook points exist for lookup/insert/evict and can emit outcome classification + cached_tokens.
- Ethan/Amara/Mina: confirm gateway attribution fields available and stable across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Sergio: draft dashboard panels; list exact fields needed + which ones can be Tier 1 vs Tier 2.

Notes to self (cleanup later)
- Keep a “metric mapping sheet” from v1 -> v2 (Mei is starting one).
- Ensure docs explicitly warn: hit_rate is not a standalone KPI; interpret with eligible_rate + saved_prefill_ms.
- Add a small section on “customer advice levers”: prompt normalization, pin models/versions, consolidate routes, adjust cache policy thresholds.
